correctness.rationale: Because each cactus cycle lies in exactly one block, the acyclic-subset partition function and random restrictions factor over bridge/cycle blocks. Every two-vertex connectivity is a product of local route-block connectivity indicators along the unique block-incidence path. For a bridge, coincident traversals give positive Bernoulli variance. For a cycle, condition independent open edges on at least one failed arc; disjoint segment-failure odds are positive. Enumerating the 3-terminal shared-vertex and both 4-terminal pairing patterns yields strictly positive algebraic covariance numerators, including ac(a+b+c+ab+bc)>0 for 3 terminals and ac[(1+b)(1+d)(1+a+c)-1]>0 for noncrossing 4 terminals; crossing case has manifest positive remainder by coefficient comparison. Identical terminal pairs have positive variance. Independence of blocks then yields strict covariance iff routes intersect, with exact zero for disjoint routes. This is universal for positive finite weights, not asserted for arbitrary overlapping-cycle graphs.

value.rationale: This settles the fresh conjectured vertex-connectivity correlation inequality on a natural infinite structural class (cacti) at every nonzero finite weight vector; in addition, the sharp shared-block strictness/independence characterization is independently useful for graphical probabilistic dependence and cannot be read from a generic nonnegative bound.

final_claim: For the independently edge-weighted random spanning-forest law on every finite connected cactus graph at arbitrary positive fugacities, any two unordered-pair vertex connectivity indicators have covariance ≥0, and strictly >0 exactly when their block-incidence routes share a bridge/cycle block, otherwise the events are independent; the pairs may overlap.
